label: Metrization and Paracompactness
notes: Open the chapter, which spans printed pages 241 through 260. We seek necessary and sufficient conditions for a topology to come from a metric, going beyond the Urysohn sufficient condition. The key tools are local finiteness, the Nagata-Smirnov theorem, and paracompactness with its partitions of unity, central to geometry and analysis on manifolds.

label: Local Finiteness
notes: A collection of subsets is locally finite when every point has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many of them. A basis that is countably locally finite, a union of countably many locally finite families, is the right notion for general metrization. Local finiteness controls how covers behave without requiring countability of the whole space.

label: The Nagata-Smirnov Theorem
notes: The Nagata-Smirnov metrization theorem gives a complete characterization: a space is metrizable if and only if it is regular and has a basis that is countably locally finite. This removes the second-countability restriction of Urysohn and applies to spaces far larger than the separable ones, settling the metrization question in full generality.

label: Paracompactness
notes: A space is paracompact when every open cover has a locally finite open refinement. Every metrizable space is paracompact, and every paracompact Hausdorff space is normal. Paracompactness is the precise hypothesis under which partitions of unity exist, making it the foundational covering property for differential geometry.

label: Partitions of Unity
notes: A partition of unity subordinate to an open cover is a family of continuous functions summing to one, each supported within a cover element. They exist exactly on paracompact spaces and let one stitch together locally defined objects, such as metrics or differential forms, into global ones. This is their indispensable role on manifolds.

label: The Smirnov Metrization Theorem
notes: The Smirnov metrization theorem states that a space is metrizable if and only if it is paracompact, Hausdorff, and locally metrizable. This ties the chapter together, linking the covering property of paracompactness directly to metrizability. With these results the metrization problem is fully resolved.
